caption: Normal synthetic input at 50% moisture, 27 °C and 60% RH produces an 8-minute fuzzy command and zero reference command.
Dry and hot synthetic inputs produce a 40-minute fuzzy command and a 10-minute threshold-reference command.
At 85% moisture both controllers issue zero and both logical pump outputs remain off.
At exactly 30% moisture the inclusive low-moisture alert is active; the fuzzy command is 20 minutes while the strict threshold reference is zero.
At 15 s raw moisture rises to 90%, while the moving average is 30%. The safety gate stops the pump despite a nonzero 34-minute fuzzy command.
An injected fault produces unavailable sensor values, zero commands and both outputs off at 15 s.
During the 10–40 s transport outage, local control remains active at 35 s while the collector holds its stale 5 s snapshot.
Seed-7 moisture noise and the five-sample average are plotted against the same simulation clock, with separate fuzzy and reference pump intervals.
A prescribed moisture ramp from 65% to 10% drives both controllers; the plotted moisture is not affected by pump output.
The Python test bench reports 17 of 17 executed checks passed, covering selected commands, rule peaks, boundaries, timer, filtering, faults and transport-surrogate behaviour.
The separate crop experiment reports held-out dataset metrics from 1,760 training and 440 test records; this does not validate physical soil-moisture inputs.
